correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2 and unrestricted irreducible symmetric stochastic supported matrix, strict trace-inverse convexity plus rotation averaging gives a unique global invariant optimizer. Removing invariant holding strictly decreases the objective, then exact Fourier eigenvalues and an absolutely convergent Poisson-kernel identity give F_m. Finite-sum strict convexity, explicit F_m′(0)<0 and F_m(1-)=infinity establish a unique interior root, with special cases and F_m′(1/3)>0 for m>=4. Uniform scaled-derivative convergence brackets the root and gives b_m~(3/(2m))^(2/3), the exact second-order cost coefficient and the ratio 3/2. The standalone checked code passes 417 assertions including independent fraction-matrix inversions and the unweighted table; no finite tests are substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Searches across semantic mathematical records, published graph-family results and primary papers identify generic Kemeny optimization, unweighted Möbius-ladder Kirchhoff indices, and a different SLEM optimum. The exact unrestricted minimizing rung probability, unique interior root and two-thirds asymptotic law do not follow from their inspected statements without new spectral and convex analysis. value.rationale: A natural infinite family of trivalent bottleneck networks, not an arbitrarily selected finite example, admits an exact unrestricted stochastic design. The sharp b~m^(-2/3) law and second-order Kemeny value separate average-hitting-time design from fastest-SLEM design (which invests m^-2 in rungs); keeping conventional equal edge probabilities loses 50% asymptotically. The exact scalar root enables independently reproducible optimal design and benchmark construction.
